stemMd: Which comparison between starch and glycogen is correct?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Starch is a protein and glycogen is a lipid.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Starch stores genetic information while glycogen catalyses reactions.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Both are glucose polymers, but glycogen is generally more highly branched.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Both are made of amino-acid monomers.

explanationMd: Starch is a major plant glucose reserve; glycogen is a glucose reserve in animals and some other organisms. Both contain glucose joined by glycosidic bonds. Glycogen has frequent branch points, providing many ends at which glucose units can be released.

distractorRationale.b: These roles confuse storage polysaccharides with nucleic acids and enzymes.
